notes: All three documents are ETSU university-layer (Board policy, Provost written guidance, Teaching Excellence syllabus guide) and both coders set delegates. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance on conditions: disclosure, citation, reflection, de-identification and verification duties were coded require or restrict by one coder; resolved to permit (condition on allowed use) or neutral (procedure), because none requires AI use. (2) Modality followed the source verb: 'Avoid' and 'should never' became should-not, 'Do not' and 'prohibited' must-not, 'should include' should, and tier descriptions in the traffic-light model informs. (3) Policy type: stay-informed duties (A used P54/P63, B UNCOVERED) resolved to UNCOVERED except instructor training (P63) and the policy-consultation duty (P54); malicious-content ban to P53; applicability and definitions to P61; instructor advice to learn before setting policy to P63; 'outline what happens' to P37; listed Red-template bans to P01. (4) Phase: syllabus statements and rationale to course-start; content-production items to during-work; instructor course-material work to before-course. (5) Unit boundaries: B split one 'may use for brainstorming, feedback, revising' sentence into two (kept one) and found 33 extra statements, 29 kept (definitions, scope notes, conditions, governance facts) and 4 dropped (the purpose sentence, the 'every policy should include' lead-in, a figure pointer, and the split-off second half of the brainstorming sentence); A's 3 extras: 2 kept, and the traffic-light intro sentence dropped as redundant. Where A normalized a policy, null was used when the anchor alone states the rule; one anchor was rewritten because both coders anchored only 'is strictly prohibited'.
